proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(A=\bar\kappa-2\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:exponent\text{-}window}\),
\[
 \epsilon\leq \alpha=\kappa-2\leq A.
 \tag{1}
\]
We first verify normalization and support.  Cartesian integration gives
\[
 \int_D \frac{\alpha+1}{4}|r|^\alpha\,dr\,ds
 =\frac{\alpha+1}{4}\frac{2}{\alpha+1}\,2=1.
 \tag{2}
\]
By the vertical-slice definition, \(V_{\mathrm{disk}}\) is the Lebesgue
area of the unit disk.  For \(0\leq\rho\leq1\),
\(1-\rho^\alpha=\int_\rho^1\alpha t^{\alpha-1}\,dt\).  Integrating this
nonnegative identity first over the disk and then over its nonnegative layer
parameter, and using the quadratic scaling of planar Lebesgue measure, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
4-Z_\alpha
 &=\int_{\{z:\|z\|_2\leq1\}}(1-\|z\|_2^\alpha)\,dz\\
 &=\int_0^1\alpha t^{\alpha-1}
      \operatorname{Leb}\{z:\|z\|_2\leq t\}\,dt\\
 &=V_{\mathrm{disk}}\int_0^1\alpha t^{\alpha+1}\,dt
 =V_{\mathrm{disk}}\frac{\alpha}{\alpha+2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
This proves the asserted normalizer.  The integrand defining \(Z_\alpha\)
is at most one.  On the set \(\{(r,s)\in D:|r|\geq1/2\}\), which has area
two, it is at least \(2^{-\alpha}\).  Hence
\[
 2^{1-\alpha}\leq Z_\alpha\leq4.
 \tag{4}
\]
Thus both formulas in \(\mathrm{def:flat\text{-}densities}\) are
nonnegative Borel densities of integral one.  The pervasive density is
positive off the line \(r=0\), and the isolated density is positive off the
origin.  Every nonempty relatively open subset of \(D\) contains a
positive-area subset avoiding the respective null set, so every such open
set has positive mass.  Both score laws consequently have support exactly
\(D\).

Fix \(x=(0,s_0)\in B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\leq h_0\).  Since
\(|s_0|\leq1/2\) and \(h_0\leq1/8\), the closed radius-\(h\) ball about
\(x\) lies in \(D\), including when \(s_0=\pm1/2\).  Its points have norm
at most \(|s_0|+h\leq5/8\), so the clipping in the isolated density is
inactive there.  Reflection in \(r=0\) shows that the two one-sided masses
are equal; the different convention on the line itself is immaterial by
absolute continuity.

For the pervasive density, vertical Cartesian slices yield
\[
 q_t^{\mathrm{perv}}(x,h)
 =\frac{\alpha+1}{2}\int_0^h r^\alpha\sqrt{h^2-r^2}\,dr
 =C_\alpha h^{\alpha+2}=C_\alpha h^\kappa.
 \tag{5}
\]
The relevant half-ball contains the rectangle
\(0\leq|r|\leq h/2\), \(|s-s_0|\leq h/2\), and is contained in the
rectangle \(0\leq|r|\leq h\), \(|s-s_0|\leq h\).  Both rectangles remain
in \(D\) at the endpoints of \(B\).  Integrating over them gives
\[
 \frac{\alpha+1}{4}h\int_0^{h/2}r^\alpha\,dr
 =2^{-\alpha-3}h^\kappa
 \leq q_t^{\mathrm{perv}}(x,h)
 \leq \frac{\alpha+1}{4}(2h)\int_0^h r^\alpha\,dr
 =\frac12h^\kappa.
 \tag{6}
\]

For the isolated density, use on the relevant side the rectangle
\(h/2\leq|r|\leq3h/4\), \(|s-s_0|\leq h/4\).  It has area \(h^2/8\),
lies in the radius-\(h\) ball because
\((3/4)^2+(1/4)^2<1\), and has \(\|z\|_2\geq h/2\).  Equation (4) gives
\[
 q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(x,h)
 \geq \frac1{Z_\alpha}\frac{h^2}{8}\left(\frac h2\right)^\alpha
 \geq2^{-\alpha-5}h^\kappa.
 \tag{7}
\]
Conversely, the half-ball has area at most \(2h^2\), and
\(\|z\|_2\leq|s_0|+h\) there.  The lower bound on \(Z_\alpha\) in (4)
therefore implies
\[
 q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(x,h)
 \leq2^{\alpha-1}\,2h^2(|s_0|+h)^\alpha
 =2^\alpha h^2(|s_0|+h)^\alpha.
 \tag{8}
\]
If \(|s_0|\geq2h\), the rectangle
\(0\leq|r|\leq h/2\), \(|s-s_0|\leq h/2\) is inside the half-ball, has
area \(h^2/2\), and satisfies
\(\|z\|_2\geq|s_0|-h/2\geq|s_0|/2\).  Using \(Z_\alpha\leq4\),
\[
 q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(x,h)
 \geq\frac14\frac{h^2}{2}
       \left(\frac{|s_0|}{2}\right)^\alpha
 =2^{-\alpha-3}h^2|s_0|^\alpha.
 \tag{9}
\]

At the origin, the same nonnegative layer calculation as in (3) gives
\[
 \int_{\{\|z\|_2\leq1\}}\|z\|_2^\alpha\,dz
 =V_{\mathrm{disk}}-
   V_{\mathrm{disk}}\frac{\alpha}{\alpha+2}
 =\frac{2V_{\mathrm{disk}}}{\alpha+2}.
\]
Scaling by \(h\), taking one half by reflection, and dividing by
\(Z_\alpha\) yield
\[
 q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(0,h)
 =\frac{V_{\mathrm{disk}}}{(\alpha+2)Z_\alpha}h^{\alpha+2}
 =D_\alpha h^\kappa.
 \tag{10}
\]

We next verify every profile condition.  By (1), (6), and (7), both score
laws obey
\[
 q_t(x,h)\geq2^{-A-5}h^\kappa=c_mh^\kappa.
 \tag{11}
\]
For the pervasive law, (6) and \(C_m=2^A+1>1/2\) show that every site of
\(B\) is thin at level \(C_mh^\kappa\).  The points
\(s_j=-1/2+jh\), \(0\leq j\leq\lfloor1/h\rfloor\), are \(h\)-separated,
and an \(h\)-separated subset of an interval of length one has at most
\(\lfloor1/h\rfloor+1\) points.  Hence
\[
 J_{P^{0,\mathrm{perv}}}(h,C_mh^\kappa)
 =\lfloor1/h\rfloor+1\geq h^{-1}=c_Jh^{-1}.
 \tag{12}
\]
For the isolated law, (8) at \(s_0=0\) gives
\(q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(0,h)\leq2^\alpha h^\kappa<C_mh^\kappa\), so the
origin is a thin site for every admitted \(h\).

For the full isolated envelope, suppose
\(a_{P^{0,\mathrm{iso}}}((0,s_0),h)\leq u\).  The side masses are equal.
By (9), either \(|s_0|<2h\), or
\[
 |s_0|\leq2\,8^{1/\alpha}
 \left(\frac{u}{h^2}\right)^{1/\alpha}.
 \tag{13}
\]
Thus the thin set is contained in a centered interval of radius
\[
 R=2h+2\,8^{1/\alpha}
 \left(\frac{u}{h^2}\right)^{1/\alpha}.
\]
An \(h\)-separated subset of an interval of radius \(R\) has at most
\(1+2R/h\) elements.  Since \(\alpha\geq\epsilon\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 J_{P^{0,\mathrm{iso}}}(h,u)
 &\leq5+4\,8^{1/\alpha}h^{-1}
       \left(\frac{u}{h^2}\right)^{1/\alpha}\\
 &\leq\left(5+4\cdot8^{1/\epsilon}\right)
 \left\{1+h^{-1}
       \left(\frac{u}{h^2}\right)^{1/\alpha}\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
This was derived for every \(u\geq0\), so it applies throughout the
required interval \(C_mh^\kappa\leq u\leq1\), including \(u=1\).
Equations (11)--(14) and the class definitions prove all score-profile
membership assertions.

We now construct the full-data laws and their conditional kernels.  For each
score density, take the product of its Borel probability measure with two
standard Gaussian measures.  Let \(X,Z_0,Z_1\) be the coordinate maps, and
apply the Borel formulas in \(\mathrm{def:gaussian\text{-}tents}\) to define
\(T,Y(0),Y(1),Y\).  Pushforward by these Borel maps gives a Borel full-data
law.  Sharp assignment and consistency hold pointwise.  The regular
conditional law of \((Y(0),Y(1))\) given \(X=z\) is the product of the two
Gaussian kernels with the displayed Borel means, so all conditional means
below are legitimate Borel representatives.

Under a baseline law, \(m_{0,P}=m_{1,P}=0\).  Under a tent law,
\[
 m_{1,P}(z)=a_{\mathrm{tent}}\psi_{j,h}(z),
 \qquad
 m_{0,P}(z)=-a_{\mathrm{tent}}\psi_{j,h}(z).
 \tag{15}
\]
The distance map and positive-part map are one-Lipschitz, so
\(\psi_{j,h}\) is \(h^{-1}\)-Lipschitz.  Since
\(a_{\mathrm{tent}}=Lh/4\), each mean in (15) is \(L/4\)-Lipschitz and
therefore \(L\)-Lipschitz on the required neighborhood.  Its boundary
trace is bounded by
\(a_{\mathrm{tent}}\leq Lh_0/4\leq L/32<L\).  Conditional on \((X,T)\),
the centered observed error is
\(\sigma\{TZ_1+(1-T)Z_0\}\); independence gives, for every
\(\lambda\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 E\!\left[
 e^{\lambda\sigma\{TZ_1+(1-T)Z_0\}}\mid X,T\right]
 =e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2/2}.
 \tag{16}
\]
Thus all baseline and tent laws obey the required smoothness, envelope, and
conditional sub-Gaussian conditions.  A tent changes no score marginal, so
(11)--(14) put every tent law in the same profile class as its baseline.
At the active center \(x_j\), (15) gives
\[
 \|\tau_{P^{j,h}}-\tau_{P^0}\|_\infty
 \geq\tau_{P^{j,h}}(x_j)-\tau_{P^0}(x_j)
 =2a_{\mathrm{tent}}=Lh/2.
 \tag{17}
\]

It remains to calculate the exact information coefficients.  Put
\(d(z)=\|z-x_j\|_2\).  From (5), for \(0\leq t\leq h\), the pervasive
score law satisfies
\[
 P^{0,\mathrm{perv}}\{d(X)\leq t\}=2C_\alpha t^\kappa.
\]
The layer identity
\[
 (1-d/h)_+^2=\int_d^h\frac2h(1-t/h)\,dt
\]
is interpreted as zero when \(d>h\).  Integrating this nonnegative layer
identity against the score law and using the preceding ball probability gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \int_D\psi_{j,h}^2f_{\mathrm{perv},\alpha}
 &=\int_0^h\frac2h(1-t/h)\,2C_\alpha t^\kappa\,dt\\
 &=\frac{4C_\alpha}{(\kappa+1)(\kappa+2)}h^\kappa
 =Q_{\mathrm{perv},\alpha}h^\kappa,
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
\]
because \(\kappa+1=\alpha+3\) and
\(\kappa+2=\alpha+4\).  At the centered isolated site, (10) gives
\(P^{0,\mathrm{iso}}\{\|X\|_2\leq t\}=2D_\alpha t^\kappa\), and the same
calculation yields
\[
 \int_D\psi_{0,h}^2f_{\mathrm{iso},\alpha}
 =Q_{\mathrm{iso},\alpha}h^\kappa.
 \tag{19}
\]

Under a tent law, the conditional observed mean relative to the baseline is
\(\mu_j(X,T)=(2T-1)a_{\mathrm{tent}}\psi_{j,h}(X)\).  Direct integration
of two Gaussian densities with common variance \(\sigma^2\) gives
conditional divergence \(\mu_j(X,T)^2/(2\sigma^2)\).  The score and
treatment laws are the same under the baseline and alternative.  Hence (18)
and \(a_{\mathrm{tent}}^2=L^2h^2/16\) imply
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P^{j,h,\mathrm{perv}}_{\mathrm{obs}},
                    P^{0,\mathrm{perv}}_{\mathrm{obs}})
 =\frac{L^2Q_{\mathrm{perv},\alpha}}{32\sigma^2}
   h^{\kappa+2}.
 \tag{20}
\]
Under independent sampling, likelihood ratios multiply, their logarithms
add, and expectation is linear.  Thus
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(
 (P^{j,h,\mathrm{perv}}_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},
 (P^{0,\mathrm{perv}}_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n}\right)
 =\frac{nL^2Q_{\mathrm{perv},\alpha}}{32\sigma^2}
   h^{\kappa+2}.
 \tag{21}
\]
Replacing (18) by (19) proves the centered isolated formula.

All constants are uniform on \(K\).  Indeed, (4), (6), (7), and (10) bound
\(Z_\alpha,C_\alpha,D_\alpha\) above and away from zero using only
\(\epsilon\) and \(A\); division by
\((\alpha+3)(\alpha+4)\) does the same for both \(Q\)-coefficients.  The
class constants are the fixed values in the proposition.  Finally, when
\(\kappa=3\), \(\alpha=1\) and
\[
 C_1=\int_0^1w\sqrt{1-w^2}\,dw=\frac13,
 \qquad
 Q_{\mathrm{perv},1}=\frac{4(1/3)}{4\cdot5}=\frac1{15}.
\]
Substitution in (21) gives
\(nL^2h^5/(480\sigma^2)\), as claimed.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \((\mathcal V,d)\) be a metric space, let \(Q_0,Q_1\) be probability
laws, and let \(v_0,v_1\in\mathcal V\) satisfy
\(d(v_0,v_1)\geq2\delta\).  If
\(\operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)\leq1/8\), then every measurable estimator
\(\widehat v\) satisfies
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}E_{Q_j}d(\widehat v,v_j)\geq\delta/4.
\]

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \((\mathcal V,d)\) be a metric space, let
\(Q_0,Q_1,\ldots,Q_M\) be probability laws with \(M\geq2\), and let
\(v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_M\in\mathcal V\) satisfy
\(d(v_j,v_k)\geq2\delta\) whenever \(j\ne k\).  If
\[
 \frac1M\sum_{j=1}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)
 \leq a\log M,
 \qquad 0<a<1/8,
\]
then every measurable estimator \(\widehat v\) satisfies
\[
 \max_{0\leq j\leq M}E_{Q_j}d(\widehat v,v_j)
 \geq \delta\frac{\sqrt M}{1+\sqrt M}
 \left(1-2a-\sqrt{\frac{2a}{\log M}}\right).
\]

added_lemmas.statement:
For each \(n\), let \(\mathfrak E_n\) be the class of all estimators
\(\widetilde\tau_n\) based on \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) for which every displayed
supremum loss is measurable.  There are constants \(c>0\) and
\(N<\infty\), depending only on the fixed class constants and uniform over
\(\kappa\in K\), such that, for every \(n\geq N\),
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau_n\in\mathfrak E_n}
 \sup_{P\in\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa}
 E_P\|\widetilde\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \geq c n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}
\]
and
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau_n\in\mathfrak E_n}
 \sup_{P\in\mathrm{Perv}_\kappa}
 E_P\|\widetilde\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \geq c\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
These endpoint benchmarks and the Le Cam--Fano route are attributed to
\(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_thickness\_estimability\_frontier/thm:thickness-entropy-separation}\)
and
\(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_thickness\_estimability\_frontier/lem:fano-tent-validity}\);
the present result re-establishes them for the normalized flat witnesses and
does not claim the converse as new.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The parent results
\(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_thickness\_estimability\_frontier/thm:thickness-entropy-separation}\)
and
\(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_thickness\_estimability\_frontier/lem:fano-tent-validity}\)
motivate the route, but they are not used as premises: we verify the testing
experiments directly from \(\mathrm{prop:flat\text{-}witness\text{-}validity}\).
An estimator having infinite expected supremum loss under one of the finite
testing laws already satisfies the desired lower bound.  Otherwise its sample
paths may be regarded, modulo null sets under those laws, as elements of the
bounded-function metric space on \(B\) with distance
\(d(f,g)=\|f-g\|_\infty\); hence the two cited metric testing inequalities
apply without a continuity restriction on the estimator.
Put \(A=\bar\kappa-2\).  The proposition's uniform-coefficient conclusion
gives a finite constant \(q_+\), depending only on the fixed exponent
window, such that
\[
 \max\{Q_{\mathrm{iso},\alpha},Q_{\mathrm{perv},\alpha}\}
 \leq q_+,
 \qquad \epsilon\leq\alpha\leq A.
 \tag{22}
\]

For the isolated experiment, choose \(0<\eta_I\leq1\) so that
\[
 \frac{L^2q_+}{32\sigma^2}\eta_I^{4+\epsilon}\leq\frac18,
 \tag{23}
\]
and set \(h_I=\eta_I n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\).  Compactness of the exponent
window implies that, for all \(n\) above one constant independent of
\(\kappa\), \(h_I\leq\min\{h_0,1/3\}\).  Take the isolated baseline and
the centered isolated tent at radius \(h_I\).  The exact membership part of
\(\mathrm{prop:flat\text{-}witness\text{-}validity}\) puts both laws in
\(\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa\).  Its separation and product-divergence conclusions
give
\[
 \|\tau_{P^{1,h_I}}-\tau_{P^0}\|_\infty\geq\frac{Lh_I}{2}
 \tag{24}
\]
and, because \(\eta_I\leq1\) and
\(\kappa+2\geq4+\epsilon\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(
 (P^{1,h_I,\mathrm{iso}}_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},
 (P^{0,\mathrm{iso}}_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n}\right)
 &=\frac{nL^2Q_{\mathrm{iso},\alpha}}{32\sigma^2}
   h_I^{\kappa+2}\\
 &\leq\frac{L^2q_+}{32\sigma^2}\eta_I^{4+\epsilon}
 \leq\frac18.
\end{aligned}
\tag{25}
\]
Apply \(\mathrm{lem:le\text{-}cam\text{-}two\text{-}point\text{-}risk}\)
with the metric \(d(f,g)=\|f-g\|_\infty\) and
\(\delta=Lh_I/4\).  Equations (24)--(25) imply, for every admissible
estimator,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa}
 E_P\|\widetilde\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \geq \frac{Lh_I}{16}
 =\frac{L\eta_I}{16}n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}.
 \tag{26}
\]
Taking the infimum proves the isolated assertion.

For the pervasive experiment, choose a constant
\(0<\eta_P\leq1/3\), to be fixed below, and put
\[
 h_P=\eta_P\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)},
 \qquad
 M=\left\lfloor\frac1{3h_P}\right\rfloor+1.
 \tag{27}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), uniformly over \(K\),
\(h_P\leq\min\{h_0,1/3\}\) and \(M\geq2\).  The points
\[
 x_j=\left(0,-\frac12+3h_P(j-1)\right),
 \qquad 1\leq j\leq M,
 \tag{28}
\]
belong to \(B\) and are \(3h_P\)-separated.  Let \(P^0\) be the pervasive
baseline and \(P^j\) the tent law at \(x_j\).  Exact membership in
\(\mathrm{Perv}_\kappa\) for the baseline and every alternative again
follows from \(\mathrm{prop:flat\text{-}witness\text{-}validity}\).

At \(x_j\), the \(j\)-th causal trace equals \(Lh_P/2\).  If \(k\ne j\),
then \(\|x_j-x_k\|_2\geq3h_P>h_P\), so the \(k\)-th tent vanishes at
\(x_j\).  Consequently, including the baseline as index zero,
\[
 \|\tau_{P^j}-\tau_{P^k}\|_\infty\geq\frac{Lh_P}{2},
 \qquad 0\leq j<k\leq M.
 \tag{29}
\]
The integer definition in (27) also gives \(M\geq(3h_P)^{-1}\).  Because
\(\kappa+2\leq\bar\kappa+2\) and \(-\log(3\eta_P)\geq0\), for all
sufficiently large \(n\), uniformly in \(\kappa\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \log M
 &\geq \frac{\log n-\log\log n}{\kappa+2}
       -\log(3\eta_P)\\
 &\geq\frac{\log n}{2(\bar\kappa+2)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{30}
\]
For each \(j\geq1\), the exact flat product-divergence identity and (22)
give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(
 (P^j_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},
 (P^0_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n}\right)
 &\leq\frac{L^2q_+}{32\sigma^2}
       n h_P^{\kappa+2}\\
 &=\frac{L^2q_+}{32\sigma^2}
       \eta_P^{\kappa+2}\log n\\
 &\leq\frac{L^2q_+}{32\sigma^2}
       \eta_P^{4+\epsilon}\log n.
\end{aligned}
\tag{31}
\]
Choose \(\eta_P\) small enough, as a function only of the fixed class
constants, that
\[
 \frac{L^2q_+}{32\sigma^2}\eta_P^{4+\epsilon}
 \leq\frac1{32(\bar\kappa+2)}.
 \tag{32}
\]
Equations (30)--(32) then imply
\[
 \frac1M\sum_{j=1}^M
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(
 (P^j_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},
 (P^0_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n}\right)
 \leq\frac1{16}\log M.
 \tag{33}
\]
Apply \(\mathrm{lem:fano\text{-}multiple\text{-}testing\text{-}risk}\)
with \(a=1/16\), the sup norm, and \(\delta=Lh_P/4\).  The parenthetical
factor in that lemma is bounded below by a positive numerical constant for
all \(M\geq2\).  From (29) and (33), there is a numerical \(c_F>0\) such
that every admissible estimator obeys
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathrm{Perv}_\kappa}
 E_P\|\widetilde\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \geq c_F\frac{Lh_P}{4}
 =c_F\frac{L\eta_P}{4}
   \left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
 \tag{34}
\]
The sampling assumption identifies each experiment in (25) and (31) with
the law of the observed iid sample.  All choices and the threshold on \(n\)
depend only on \(L,\sigma,h_0,\epsilon,\bar\kappa\) and the fixed class
constants, not on \(\kappa\).  Taking the infimum in (34), and then the
smaller of the constants in (26) and (34), completes both uniform minimax
lower bounds.

prose_updates.tldr: One explicit total global-bandwidth severity-net estimator, using neither \(\kappa\) nor a regime label, simultaneously attains the exact isolated minimax order \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\), the exact pervasive minimax order \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), and the classical regular-design upper rate \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\). The endpoint converses are re-established with normalized flat Gaussian-tent laws and attributed to the banked parent; the novelty is simultaneous cross-regime attainment by the same estimator, not a new lower-bound or regular-log frontier.

project_justification.gap: The isolated and pervasive endpoint minimax orders were available as banked-parent benchmarks, but a single measurable causal-trace estimator had not been shown to attain both orders, together with the regular positive-density rate, without knowing the mass exponent or a regime label.
project_justification.niche: The contribution is the global-bandwidth empirical severity-net oracle on the declared bivariate side-mass classes and its simultaneous evaluation on regular, isolated, and pervasive designs. Exact flat-law Le Cam and Fano experiments certify the two depleted endpoint converses, but those converses and the classical regular logarithmic benchmark are supporting, attributed results rather than novelty claims.
project_justification.fill: Lower-mass bands and ordered greedy anchors control the conditional maximum through \(1\vee J_P\). Evaluating the unchanged \(\inf_h\sup_x\) oracle at the isolated, pervasive, and regular balances gives all three upper rates for the identical total estimator. The normalized flat baseline and Gaussian tents independently recover the attributed isolated and pervasive lower orders on the same law classes.

prose_updates.related_work: The downgraded banked parent \(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_thickness\_estimability\_frontier}\) supplied the isolated and pervasive endpoint benchmarks and the Le Cam--Fano architecture using circular witnesses. The present supporting converse rebuilds those benchmarks with normalized Cartesian and clipped radial-power flat laws; it is not claimed as new. The accepted-bank comparator \(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_uniform\_log\_penalty\_v1}\) owns the boundary uniform-log results on its CTY-derived decision and law triples: a \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\) converse on its full \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\) problem and a matched outer-expected frontier on its distinct displayed \(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) specialization in the stated parameter regime. This note does not reclaim that regular logarithmic benchmark; it adds one total severity-net estimator that also adapts to polynomially depleted isolated and pervasive designs. A continuous score density bounded below near \(B\) implies the present regular side-mass condition, but only the conditionally \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian, envelope-compatible laws with matching frozen constants form a verified overlap. No broader class inclusion or converse transfer is asserted without the same loss and unrestricted estimator class. Gaiffas (2005, 2007, 2009) studies univariate pointwise or spatially normalized inhomogeneous regression; dimension, causal target, and loss differ, so product embeddings can support lower submodels but not upper-theorem transfer.
prose_updates.interpretation: The normalized flat experiments show that an isolated thin site costs \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\), whereas order \(h^{-1}\) simultaneously thin sites force the additional supremum logarithm and the rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\). The same first-half severity net and one selected global bandwidth attain both exact orders; on regular side mass they also attain the classical \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\) upper rate. The exact depleted rates are therefore minimax benchmarks, while the paper's new content is one-procedure simultaneous attainment.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The oracle is deliberately global-bandwidth: its optimization order is \(\inf_h\sup_x\), not \(\sup_x\inf_h\). The result does not claim arbitrary-profile local-oracle exactness, point-dependent bandwidth adaptation, or any confidence band or expected-width guarantee. The finite selector, packing event, and anchor construction are estimator components only. Constants are uniform only on the compact exponent window bounded away from two.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The delivered result concerns expected supremum risk for one explicit total estimator on three law-defined regimes: regular side mass, isolated thinning, and pervasive thinning. The isolated and pervasive rates are matched by flat-law lower bounds, but those endpoint converses are attributed to the banked parent; the regular logarithmic benchmark belongs to the accepted-bank CTY-derived comparator. Novelty is limited to simultaneous attainment of the three upper rates by the same global-bandwidth severity-net estimator, which uses neither \(\kappa\) nor a regime label. Comparator transfer is asserted only on an exact common subclass with matching assumptions, loss, and estimator quantifiers. The withdrawn confidence-band and expected-width program is not delivered, and no finite selector, packing event, or anchor is relabeled as a band.

added_lemmas.statement:
There exist constants \(c>0\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\), depending only on the fixed class constants and on the compact exponent window \(K\), such that, simultaneously for every \(\kappa\in K\) and every \(n\geq n_0\),
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa}
 E_P\|\widetilde\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \geq c n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}
\]
and
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathrm{Perv}_\kappa}
 E_P\|\widetilde\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \geq c\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
Each infimum is over all estimators \(\widetilde\tau_n\) mapping the observed sample space \((D\times\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R)^n\) to bounded real functions on \(B\), with jointly Borel coordinate map and measurable supremum loss.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(A=\bar\kappa-2\), so the exponent-window assumption gives
\[
 \epsilon\leq\alpha=\kappa-2\leq A.
 \tag{L1}
\]
The uniformity conclusion of \(\mathrm{prop{:}flat\text{-}witness\text{-}validity}\) implies that
\[
 0<\overline Q:=
 \sup_{\alpha\in[\epsilon,A]}
 \max\{Q_{\mathrm{iso},\alpha},Q_{\mathrm{perv},\alpha}\}<\infty.
 \tag{L2}
\]
Set \(A_\star=L^2\overline Q/(32\sigma^2)\).

We first record an elementary two-experiment inequality, deriving the testing step used below.  Let \(Q_0,Q_1\) be two probability laws, let \(v_0,v_1\) be two elements of a metric space with distance \(\Delta=d(v_0,v_1)>0\), and let \(\widehat v\) be any measurable estimator.  Define the nearest-point test
\[
 \phi=\mathbf 1\{d(\widehat v,v_1)\leq d(\widehat v,v_0)\}.
\]
The triangle inequality shows that \(d(\widehat v,v_0)\geq\Delta/2\) on \(\{\phi=1\}\), and that \(d(\widehat v,v_1)\geq\Delta/2\) on \(\{\phi=0\}\).  Consequently
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}E_{Q_j}d(\widehat v,v_j)
 \geq \frac{\Delta}{4}
 \{Q_0(\phi=1)+Q_1(\phi=0)\}
 \geq\frac{\Delta}{4}\{1-\|Q_1-Q_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\}.
 \tag{L3}
\]
To obtain a KL-only lower bound without importing another premise, take densities \(p_0,p_1\) with respect to a common dominating measure and put \(\rho=\int\sqrt{p_0p_1}\).  Jensen's inequality under \(Q_1\) gives
\[
 \log\rho
 =\log E_{Q_1}\sqrt{p_0/p_1}
 \geq-\frac12\operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0).
 \tag{L4}
\]
The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality gives
\[
 \|Q_1-Q_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \leq\frac12
 \left(\int(\sqrt{p_1}-\sqrt{p_0})^2\right)^{1/2}
 \left(\int(\sqrt{p_1}+\sqrt{p_0})^2\right)^{1/2}
 =\sqrt{1-\rho^2}.
 \tag{L5}
\]
Thus, if \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)\leq1/8\), equations \((\mathrm{L3})\)--\((\mathrm{L5})\) imply
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}E_{Q_j}d(\widehat v,v_j)
 \geq c_{\mathrm{test}}\Delta,
 \qquad
 c_{\mathrm{test}}:=\frac{1-\sqrt{1-e^{-1/8}}}{4}>0.
 \tag{L6}
\]

For the isolated experiment, define the constant
\[
 \eta_{\mathrm I}
 =\min\left\{h_0,\frac13,1,(8A_\star)^{-1/(4+\epsilon)}\right\}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 h=\eta_{\mathrm I}n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}.
 \tag{L7}
\]
Use the isolated baseline \(P^{0,\mathrm{iso}}\) and its centered tent law \(P^{0,h,\mathrm{iso}}\) from \(\mathrm{def{:}gaussian\text{-}tents}\).  The exact membership conclusion of \(\mathrm{prop{:}flat\text{-}witness\text{-}validity}\) puts both laws in \(\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa\).  The same proposition gives target separation
\[
 \Delta_{\mathrm I}
 =\|\tau_{P^{0,h,\mathrm{iso}}}-
       \tau_{P^{0,\mathrm{iso}}}\|_\infty
 \geq \frac{Lh}{2}
 \tag{L8}
\]
and the exact product divergence
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(
 (P^{0,h,\mathrm{iso}}_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},
 (P^{0,\mathrm{iso}}_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n}\right)
 =\frac{nL^2Q_{\mathrm{iso},\alpha}h^{\kappa+2}}{32\sigma^2}
 \leq A_\star\eta_{\mathrm I}^{\kappa+2}
 \leq\frac18.
 \tag{L9}
\]
The last inequality uses \(\eta_{\mathrm I}\leq1\), \(\kappa+2\geq4+\epsilon\), and the definition in \((\mathrm{L7})\).  Applying \((\mathrm{L6})\) with the supremum norm, and observing that the supremum over \(\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa\) dominates the maximum over these two members, yields for every estimator
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa}
 E_P\|\widetilde\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \geq \frac{c_{\mathrm{test}}L\eta_{\mathrm I}}{2}
 n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}.
 \tag{L10}
\]
Taking the infimum over all measurable estimators proves the isolated lower bound.

For the pervasive experiment, put
\[
 \eta_{\mathrm P}
 =\min\left\{h_0,\frac1{12},1,
 [16(\bar\kappa+2)A_\star]^{-1/(4+\epsilon)}\right\},
 \qquad
 h=\eta_{\mathrm P}\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
 \tag{L11}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), uniformly over \(\kappa\in K\), let
\[
 M=\left\lfloor\frac1{3h}\right\rfloor+1,
 \qquad
 x_j=\left(0,-\frac12+3h(j-1)\right),
 \quad 1\leq j\leq M.
 \tag{L12}
\]
These points belong to \(B\) and are \(3h\)-separated.  Let \(P_j=P^{j,h,\mathrm{perv}}\) be the corresponding tent laws and let \(P_0=P^{0,\mathrm{perv}}\) denote the pervasive baseline.  The exact membership conclusion of \(\mathrm{prop{:}flat\text{-}witness\text{-}validity}\) gives
\[
 P_0,P_1,\ldots,P_M\in\mathrm{Perv}_\kappa.
 \tag{L13}
\]
For distinct \(j,k\), the tent definition gives \(\psi_{j,h}(x_j)=1\) and \(\psi_{k,h}(x_j)=0\), because \(\|x_j-x_k\|_2\geq3h>h\).  Since the two observed-side means are shifted by opposite amounts, it follows that
\[
 \|\tau_{P_j}-\tau_{P_k}\|_\infty
 \geq |\tau_{P_j}(x_j)-\tau_{P_k}(x_j)|
 =2a_{\mathrm{tent}}=\frac{Lh}{2}
 =:\Delta_{\mathrm P}.
 \tag{L14}
\]
The exact KL identity in the witness proposition and \((\mathrm{L2})\) imply
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left((P_j^{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},
 (P_0^{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n}\right)
 \leq A_\star nh^{\kappa+2}
 =A_\star\eta_{\mathrm P}^{\kappa+2}\log n
 \leq\frac{\log n}{16(\bar\kappa+2)}.
 \tag{L15}
\]

We next derive the required finite-packing inequality.  Let \(J\) be uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,M\}\), and conditionally on \(J=j\), let \(W\) have law \((P_j^{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n}\).  Write \(\overline P=M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M(P_j^{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n}\).  Expansion of the logarithms of densities gives
\[
 \frac1M\sum_{j=1}^M
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left((P_j^{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},
 (P_0^{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n}\right)
 =I(J;W)+\operatorname{KL}\!\left(\overline P,
 (P_0^{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n}\right),
 \tag{L16}
\]
so \(I(J;W)\) is no larger than the left-hand side.  For any decision rule \(\widehat J(W)\), let \(p_e=P\{\widehat J\ne J\}\).  Conditioning additionally on the error indicator gives
\[
 H(J\mid W)\leq\log2+p_e\log(M-1)
 \leq\log2+p_e\log M.
 \tag{L17}
\]
Since \(I(J;W)=\log M-H(J\mid W)\), equations \((\mathrm{L16})\)--\((\mathrm{L17})\) yield
\[
 p_e\geq1-
 \frac{M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M
 \operatorname{KL}((P_j^{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},
                    (P_0^{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n})+\log2}
      {\log M}.
 \tag{L18}
\]

Because \(M\geq(3h)^{-1}\), equation \((\mathrm{L11})\) and \(\kappa\leq\bar\kappa\) give
\[
 \log M
 \geq\frac{\log n-\log\log n}{\bar\kappa+2}-\log3
 \geq\frac{\log n}{2(\bar\kappa+2)}
 \tag{L19}
\]
for all \(n\geq n_0\), where \(n_0\) can be chosen independently of \(\kappa\in K\).  Enlarge \(n_0\) so that also \(\log2/\log M\leq1/4\).  Equations \((\mathrm{L15})\), \((\mathrm{L18})\), and \((\mathrm{L19})\) then give \(p_e\geq5/8\).

Given an arbitrary estimator \(\widetilde\tau_n\), let \(\widehat J\) be the least index minimizing \(\|\widetilde\tau_n-\tau_{P_j}\|_\infty\).  The stipulated measurability of the supremum losses makes this finite decision rule measurable.  On \(\{\widehat J\ne j\}\), nearest-point optimality and \((\mathrm{L14})\) imply
\[
 \Delta_{\mathrm P}
 \leq\|\tau_{P_j}-\widetilde\tau_n\|_\infty
     +\|\widetilde\tau_n-\tau_{P_{\widehat J}}\|_\infty
 \leq2\|\widetilde\tau_n-\tau_{P_j}\|_\infty.
 \tag{L20}
\]
Averaging \((\mathrm{L20})\) over \(j\) and using \(p_e\geq5/8\) gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathrm{Perv}_\kappa}
 E_P\|\widetilde\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \geq\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^M
 E_{P_j}\|\widetilde\tau_n-\tau_{P_j}\|_\infty
 \geq\frac{5L\eta_{\mathrm P}}{32}
 \left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
 \tag{L21}
\]
Taking the infimum over estimators proves the pervasive lower bound.  With
\[
 c=\min\left\{\frac{c_{\mathrm{test}}L\eta_{\mathrm I}}2,
                   \frac{5L\eta_{\mathrm P}}{32}\right\}>0,
\]
the same constant applies to both conclusions.  The constants \(\eta_{\mathrm I}\), \(\eta_{\mathrm P}\), \(c_{\mathrm{test}}\), and \(n_0\) depend only on \(K,h_0,L,\sigma\) and the uniformly bounded witness coefficients, so both bounds are uniform over \(\kappa\in K\).
added_lemmas.justification: This supporting converse records the exact isolated Le Cam and pervasive finite-packing benchmarks attributed to the banked parent analysis.
added_lemmas.gap: The benchmark rates are supporting converses; the present note's new claim is simultaneous attainment by one total severity-net estimator.
added_lemmas.consumer: The same-estimator endpoint corollary uses these lower bounds to certify minimax-order attainment in both depleted-design regimes.

proposed.statement:
Corollary (same-estimator consequence for the endpoint classes of \(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_thickness\_estimability\_frontier}\)). There is a finite constant \(C\), uniform over \(K\), such that for every \(\kappa\in K\) and all sufficiently large \(n\), the single total estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\), without knowledge of \(\kappa\) or the endpoint class, satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa}E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \leq Cn^{-1/(\kappa+2)},
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathrm{Perv}_\kappa}E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \leq C(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
proposed.justification: Common bandwidths at the isolated and pervasive balances evaluate the corrected oracle without changing either endpoint exponent.
proposed.gap: The missing step was simultaneous attainment by one profile-free estimator, not the endpoint rate calculation itself.
proposed.consumer: Together with the regular-design corollary, the proposition gives one deployable procedure across all three named regimes.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the mandated exact endpoint converse into the endpoint adaptation corollary while leaving its existing upper-bound claim unchanged.
